$comment: Runnable eval definitions for /handoff. Converted from this file's own pre-harness shape (bare integer ids, `name`/`assertions`/`files`, prose `fixture`) into the per-skill harness schema in docs/strategy-skill-evals.md §3 — issue #585, decisions recorded there. EXECUTION NOTICE: skill-eval prompts are never executed against the real repo or real GitHub — any skill, any origin. `kind: execution` entries require a harness-built sandbox (`fixture` names the starting-state profile in scripts/skill-evals/lib/fixtures.mjs) — see docs/strategy-skill-evals.md. /handoff has no `kind: routing` evals; whether it gains any is a separate decision (#507). FIXTURE COVERAGE: four profiles were built for this skill (handoff-1, -4, -7, -8). The other six name one of those and state in their own `notes` exactly how the profile's world differs from the `preconditions` above it — under §3's rule the prose is the contract and the profile is its implementation, so where they disagree the profile is the gap, not the prose. The worlds no profile implements are still described, file by file, in the pre-harness builder .claude/skills/handoff/evals/build_fixtures.mjs, which is kept as that record and is NOT the way to run an eval. CONVERSATION CLAIMS: several evals turn on the human believing something that git/gh contradicts. Where the prompt is natural language the claim is in the prompt itself; where the prompt is a slash invocation it is attributed in `preconditions`, to be put into the executor's task framing. Design and rationale: docs/design-skill-evals-harness.md.

evals.prompt: Hopping on a call in 5 min — can you throw together a hand-off for the notifier retry-count fix? Pretty sure I already committed it earlier, just need something I can hand to a fresh session after lunch.
evals.preconditions: Branch 486-notifier-retry-fix, no commits ahead of main. src/server/notifier.ts modified but uncommitted (the retry-count change). No PR. The human's stale belief — that the change was already committed — is carried in the prompt itself.
evals.expected_output: A .scratch/*-bootstrap.md hand-off doc plus a printed bootstrap prompt, at default (compact) depth. The doc must correctly report that the notifier retry-count change is NOT committed (git status shows the file modified/uncommitted) even though the user believed it was — the skill should verify via git rather than repeat the user's claim at face value.
expectations: States the notifier retry-count change is NOT committed / still shows as uncommitted in git status
Does not assert or imply the change was already committed
Created a hand-off doc file (e.g. under .scratch/) rather than only responding in chat
Doc or response lists the uncommitted file(s) explicitly
Doc stays at default depth: no decision-log table, risk register, alternatives-considered, or detailed-chronology sections
Doc includes a concrete resume/next-step section ending in one bounded next action with real commands where they matter
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt for a fresh session
Doc includes a 'How this work is done' section that names the orchestration pattern and the roles or personas involved (a one-line 'solo, no personas' answer is acceptable)
evals.notes: Profile built for this eval (#585). The produced doc is archived from the sandbox's .scratch/ by archiveEvidence, so the grader reads the document itself and not a summary of it.

evals.prompt: /handoff — we finished the drift-check workflow stub since this morning's hand-off doc, update it for whoever picks this up next.
evals.preconditions: Branch 396-pr3-drift with an existing .scratch/drift-workflow-bootstrap.md written this morning (old template: 'State as of' says PR 3 design finished, drift-check workflow drafted but not implemented). Since then: one new commit adding .github/workflows/skill-creator-drift.yml (the stub). Working tree clean.
evals.expected_output: Updates the existing .scratch/drift-workflow-bootstrap.md: preserves the prior morning-state content under a 'Historical' heading rather than deleting it, adds new current state reflecting the new commit (the drift-check workflow stub), and prints an updated bootstrap prompt.
expectations: The prior state description (PR 3 design finished / drift-check workflow drafted but not implemented) survives somewhere in the updated doc
The updated doc has a distinct heading separating prior/historical state from current state
The updated doc's current state reflects the new commit (the drift-check workflow stub now exists)
The existing doc was updated in place, not replaced by a differently-named or duplicate doc
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt reflecting the updated state
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5). `fixture` names the nearest built world, `feature-one-commit-clean-no-pr` — one commit ahead of main, clean tree, no PR — which matches the SHAPE above but not its content: there is no pre-existing .scratch/drift-workflow-bootstrap.md, and the commit is a notifier fix rather than the workflow stub. The pre-existing doc is the whole point of this eval, so NOTHING here is gradeable as written until a profile seeds one (a `working.write` of the morning doc onto this profile is all it needs). Its world is described file by file in build_fixtures.mjs (eval 2).

evals.preconditions: On main, clean working tree, no commits ahead of origin/main, no PR, no meaningful prior conversation about any workstream.
evals.human_script: None — the skill is expected to stop and ask what the hand-off is for; no scripted human reply is required for this eval to complete.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there is nothing in-flight to hand off (clean working tree, on main, no distinguishing branch work) and asks what this hand-off is for, rather than fabricating a doc about nonexistent work.
expectations: Response asks a clarifying question about what topic/work the hand-off is for, rather than proceeding blind
No hand-off doc is created that describes fabricated or invented in-flight work
Response reflects awareness that the working tree is clean / on main with nothing distinguishing in flight
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5) — and none of the eighteen builds this world, because every profile checks out a feature branch. `fixture` names the nearest clean-tree world so the reference resolves, but that sandbox sits on a feature branch one commit ahead, which is precisely the state this eval says is absent: it is NOT gradeable as written. Every other piece is now in place — #585 guarded buildSandbox's `git switch -c` with `if (profile.branch)`, so a profile that omits `branch` and stays on main builds cleanly. Adding that profile is the whole remaining cost.

evals.preconditions: Branch 486-notifier-retry-fix, one commit ahead of main ('fix(notifier): stop double-counting retries'), working tree clean, npm run test:functional passed earlier this session. No PR exists. Attributed claim to put in the executor's task framing: earlier in the session the human said 'the PR is already up'.
evals.expected_output: A genuinely minimal .scratch/notifier-retry-bootstrap.md (slug from the argument): goal+done-when compressed to a line or two, short bullets, essential anchors kept, no ceremony — plus a printed bootstrap prompt. Corrects the user's stale belief that a PR is already open.
expectations: Doc created at .scratch/notifier-retry-bootstrap.md — slug taken from the argument, mode flag not mistaken for a slug
Doc is materially low-ceremony: no decision tables, risk registers, alternatives-considered, chronology, or multi-step future plans
Essential anchors survive the contraction: branch and commit, working-tree state, and at least one key file path
Corrects the stale claim: reports that no PR exists rather than repeating that one is up
Contains a verification step and exactly one concrete next action
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
The 'How this work is done' section is present but contracted to a single line — not omitted, not expanded
evals.notes: Profile built for this eval (#585). The stale PR claim is a conversation fact, not a repo fact: the sandbox's gh stub answers `gh pr view` for this branch with 'no pull requests found', which is what makes the correction gradeable.

evals.preconditions: Branch 396-pr3-drift-workflow, three commits ahead of main. A decision-review doc .scratch/pr3-drift-roundtable.md records this session's decision: monthly scheduled drift-check workflow chosen over per-PR checking, with alternatives and reasons. Workstream A (workflow YAML + script) implemented; exit-code-2 path live-tested; functional tests pass; e2e not run. Workstream B (docs update) not started. Open PR #489 with one check still pending. Attributed claim to put in the executor's task framing: earlier in the session the human said 'CI is green on the PR'.
evals.expected_output: A full-depth .scratch/pr3-drift-bootstrap.md: decision log with rationale/evidence identifying the roundtable doc, validation split into completed vs still-required, exact stopping point, ordered resume plan with approval gate — plus a printed bootstrap prompt. Reports the PR's real (pending) check status, not the remembered 'green' claim.
expectations: Decisions are recorded with rationale and evidence, not bare conclusions
The roundtable/design-review doc is identified as the decision log
Validation separates completed checks (with their results) from still-required checks
Status identifies the exact stopping point, separating in-progress from not-started work (docs workstream)
Reports the PR check status as verified (pending), not the remembered 'green' claim
Resume plan is ordered, starts with verification/preflight, and includes an approval gate before merge
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
The 'How this work is done' section carries the roles in play, roles to add or swap next, and answers 'what gap did no role own?'
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5). `fixture` names the nearest built world, `feature-migration-open-pr-teammate-wip`, which supplies the two structural facts this eval needs — an open PR whose `statusCheckRollup` still has one check IN_PROGRESS (so the 'CI is green' claim is checkably wrong) and work split across a finished and an unfinished part. It does NOT supply the .scratch/pr3-drift-roundtable.md decision-review doc, so expectations 1, 2 and 8 (the decision-log leg, the point of this eval) are not gradeable on it; two commits, not three; different domain. Seeding the roundtable doc via `working.write` is what a purpose-built profile would add. Its world is described file by file in build_fixtures.mjs (eval 5).

evals.prompt: That's the whole fix — just leave a quick minimal handoff so tomorrow-me can close this out, nothing fancy.
evals.preconditions: Branch chore/biome-rule-tweak with one uncommitted modified file (biome.jsonc — a lint rule severity change made this session). No commits ahead of main, no PR. Tests not yet run this session.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes natural-language minimal-mode intent and proceeds (no clarifying question needed): a short handoff doc with the uncommitted file and branch anchors, the not-yet-run test as the next required check, one exact next action, and a printed bootstrap prompt.
expectations: Proceeds without asking a clarifying question — the intent and scope are clear
Minimal-depth structure: goal and completion condition compressed into one or two lines, short bullets, no Full-only ceremony sections
The uncommitted file and branch anchor are still present despite the contraction
Identifies that tests haven't been run as the next required check, and gives one exact next action
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5) — and the only one of the six reusers that loses nothing. `feature-uncommitted-fix-no-pr` is this eval's world in every respect the expectations touch: exactly one uncommitted modified file, no commits ahead of main, no PR, no tests run. Only the branch name and the file differ (486-notifier-retry-fix / src/server/notifier.ts instead of chore/biome-rule-tweak / biome.jsonc), and no expectation names either. Grade it against the sandbox's actual branch and file.

evals.prompt: Write the compact version for the buttondown-sync work — I know it's sprawling, but I just need the essentials.
evals.preconditions: Branch 512-buttondown-tag-mirror, two commits ahead of main, one modified file uncommitted. Two workstreams: tag-mirror cron fix (in progress), write-policy doc update (not started). Open question from this session: whether Buttondown rate limits require batching. Open issue #512, no PR.
evals.expected_output: Honors the explicit compact request even though the work's complexity would otherwise justify full: a compact doc that still names both workstreams and the open question, with no Full-only ceremony — plus a printed bootstrap prompt.
expectations: Document stays compact overall despite the complexity: no decision-log table, risk register, alternatives-considered, or detailed chronology
Both workstreams appear in the status (essentials are not dropped to achieve brevity)
The open rate-limit question is recorded
Compact spine intact: leads with goal and status, has verified-state anchors, ends in one concrete next action
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
evals.notes: Profile built for this eval (#585). The open rate-limit question is discoverable from the repo as well as the conversation: the uncommitted edit to src/server/buttondown.ts carries it as a TODO comment. The second workstream (the write-policy doc update) is not-started work, so it exists only in the framing above — as it does in the real session this eval models.

evals.prompt: Let's stop here for tonight — write a handoff so whoever picks this up tomorrow has what they need.
evals.preconditions: Branch 518-member-status-migration, two commits ahead of main (expand migration + new column write path). API change half-implemented: read path still on old column. Consequential decision this session: expand-contract ordering — the contract migration must NOT ship until all readers are migrated. A teammate's WIP file (src/app/members/page.tsx) is modified in the working tree — this session never touched it. Migration applied locally; preview e2e not run. Open PR #520 linked to issue #518.
evals.expected_output: No depth was specified; the recovery risk (expand-contract migration mid-flight, half-implemented API change, teammate's WIP file, unverified preview) justifies automatic full-depth treatment: decision log with rationale/evidence, separated validation states, ordered resume plan with the contract-step stop condition as a gate, ownership uncertainty recorded — plus a printed bootstrap prompt.
expectations: Escalates to full-depth treatment unprompted: decisions carry rationale and evidence, validation states are separated, resume plan is ordered
The expand-contract constraint (contract step must wait for reader migration) is recorded as a stop condition or approval gate
The teammate's modified file is listed with its uncertain/other ownership noted, without claiming it or requiring it be committed
Verified facts are distinguished from assumptions or unknowns
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
evals.notes: Profile built for this eval (#585). Three of its facts are in the repo, not just the framing: the read path is still on the old column (a comment in src/server/api.ts says so), src/app/members/page.tsx is modified in the working tree with no commit of this session's touching it, and PR #520's statusCheckRollup has E2E still IN_PROGRESS. That the teammate, not this session, made the page.tsx edit is a conversation fact — put it in the executor's task framing.

evals.preconditions: Branch 507-avatar-url-ttl, one commit ahead of main (signed-URL TTL fix) plus one modified file from this session's work (src/server/avatars.ts, uncommitted follow-up). Additionally src/lib/supabase/client.ts is modified but this session never touched it — origin unknown (possibly the user's manual edit). npm run test:functional passed after the fix.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary work with one recovery-risk wrinkle: the doc stays compact overall but expands the verified-state/working-tree area to flag the unexplained modified file and its uncertain ownership. No cascade into other Full-only sections. Printed bootstrap prompt included.
expectations: Document stays compact overall: no decision-log table, risk register, alternatives-considered, or detailed chronology appears
The verified-state/working-tree area explicitly flags the unexplained modified file and that its origin/ownership is uncertain
The unexplained file is not silently folded into the session's own work, and no commit is demanded
The expansion does not cascade: decisions and validation stay at compact depth
One concrete next action and a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt are present
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5). `fixture` names `feature-migration-open-pr-teammate-wip` because it supplies the one thing this eval turns on — a modified file in the working tree that the session did not touch and cannot account for (src/app/members/page.tsx there, src/lib/supabase/client.ts here). All five expectations are gradeable against it, reading that file as the unexplained one. What differs: two commits rather than one, an open PR where this eval has none, no second session-owned uncommitted edit, and a different domain. Its world is described file by file in build_fixtures.mjs (eval 9).

evals.prompt: I need a full handoff for the drift work — the decisions, risks, and what validation is still left. This has several moving pieces, so give the next agent everything. CI's green on the PR already, by the way.
evals.preconditions: Identical to handoff-5 (slash-full-decision-log) — the same world, deliberately. The slash/NL pair on identical state doubles as a consistency check between the two invocation interfaces; compare the two docs in the analyst pass. The human's stale 'CI is green' belief is carried in the prompt itself, this being the natural-language half of the pair.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes natural-language full-mode intent. Produces a full-depth handoff equivalent in structure to the slash-full run on the identical fixture: decision log with rationale/evidence identifying the roundtable doc, split validation, stopping point, ordered resume plan with approval gate, corrected PR check status — plus a printed bootstrap prompt.
expectations: Full-depth treatment from the natural-language modifier alone: decisions carry rationale and evidence, validation states are separated, resume plan is ordered
The roundtable/design-review doc is identified as the decision log
Reports the PR check status as verified (pending), not the remembered 'green' claim
Status identifies the exact stopping point, separating in-progress from not-started work (docs workstream)
Doc slug derived sensibly from the drift-work context (e.g. pr3-drift), not from mode words
Final chat response includes a printed, paste-ready bootstrap prompt
evals.notes: No profile of its own (#585, decision 5); it names the same profile as handoff-5 on purpose, so the pair still runs on one identical world and the slash/NL comparison survives the reuse. The same gap applies: no .scratch/pr3-drift-roundtable.md exists in that world, so expectation 2 is not gradeable on it, and expectation 5's slug is derived from the sandbox's branch rather than the drift work. The prompt carries one addition made in the conversion (#585, decision 3): the trailing 'CI's green on the PR already, by the way', which puts handoff-5's attributed claim into the prompt where the interface is natural language. Nothing else in this eval's text changed.
